programs.name: Clinical Research Office at UCSF Hyde & Stanyan Hospitals
programs.card: OCR runs the Clinical Research Office at UCSF Hyde and Stanyan Hospitals, helping UCSF investigators activate, coordinate, and enroll studies and building new collaborations with hospital physicians.
programs.full: OCR manages the Clinical Research Office (CRO) for UCSF Hyde and Stanyan Hospitals (formerly Saint Francis and St. Mary's), expanding UCSF's research mission across both hospitals and their outpatient clinics in partnership with UCSF Health Network. The CRO connects researchers with unit managers and hospital leadership; guides studies through UCSF IRB approval, Office of Clinical Trials Activation, and site-specific requirements; and provides on-site operational support, including patient recruitment and enrollment, study coordination, and clinical data collection. OCR also manages the transition of 14 existing hospital research projects to UCSF and is identifying clinical groups to launch new collaborative projects with UCSF investigators.
programs.partnerDepts: UCSF Health Network (Clinical and Medical Staff Affairs)
programs.title: UCSF Hyde & Stanyan Hospitals
programs.subtitle: Clinical Research Office

programs.name: Clinical Research Program in Bronchiectasis & NTM
programs.division: Pulmonary, Critical Care, Allergy & Sleep Medicine
programs.card: OCR provides senior clinical research coordination for the Bronchiectasis & NTM Program (INTEGRATE), supporting study startup, day-to-day study oversight, CRC training, and safety escalation across active studies.
programs.full: Through a pilot partnership launched in 2026, OCR supports the startup and operation of clinical and translational studies within INTEGRATE. A senior OCR clinical research coordinator helps activate new studies with the IRB and Office of Clinical Trials Activation, monitors progress and risks across active studies, trains and mentors junior coordinators on protocol adherence, data integrity, and Good Clinical Practice, coordinates escalation of adverse events and sponsor notifications, and helps refine study workflows and SOPs.
programs.title: Bronchiectasis & NTM
programs.subtitle: Clinical Research Program

programs.name: Clinical Research Program in Interstitial Lung Disease
programs.fullTitle: Interstitial Lung Disease (ILD) Clinical Research Program
programs.division: Pulmonary, Critical Care, Allergy & Sleep Medicine
programs.card: OCR provided clinical research oversight, coordination, and escalation support for the Interstitial Lung Disease (ILD) program, stabilizing active studies, re-engaging paused studies, and supporting new study startups.
programs.full: OCR supported the ILD Clinical Research Program with oversight and coordination of its clinical research operations. OCR held regular check-ins with study coordinators to review study status and resolve blockers; coordinated escalation of time-sensitive issues such as adverse events, sponsor and medical monitor notifications, and urgent protocol questions; guided required documentation and IRB reporting; helped re-activate paused studies through the Office of Clinical Trials Activation; and developed workflows and escalation SOPs.
programs.title: Interstitial Lung Disease
programs.subtitle: Clinical Research Program

programs.name: ImmunoX co·projects Research Program
programs.card: OCR manages the full slate of ImmunoX co·projects — collaborative pilot-to-program studies using CoLabs technology to build detailed immune profiles across diverse diseases.
programs.title: ImmunoX co·projects
programs.subtitle: Research Program

programs.name: UCSF Custom Discovery Research Platform
programs.fullTitle: UCSF Custom Discovery: A platform for personalized cancer discovery and treatment
programs.card: UCSF Custom Discovery is a platform for personalized cancer research and treatment. It profiles an individual patient's tumor and immune cells in depth to help their care team find matching existing drugs or point toward new custom therapies, in days to weeks.
programs.full: Custom Discovery, a program of the UCSF Immunoprofiler and ImmunoX, offers personalized profiling of a patient's cancer to help patients and clinicians find novel or cutting-edge therapies. Working with the patient's clinicians to ensure good sample preparation, the team applies the same methods used in the Immunoprofiler's large cohort studies, including DNA and RNA sequencing of tumor cells and the surrounding immune cells and a large CITE-seq panel, on tumor, normal tissue, and blood. A rapid track returns results in about 1 to 3 days and a deeper track in 4 to 8 weeks. Findings, shared with the patient's care team, may identify existing drugs that match the tumor's biology or support custom therapies or vaccines, and a portion of each tumor is kept frozen to test future treatments. A cross-functional team of immunologists, biostatisticians, pathologists, and project managers works closely with each patient.
programs.title: UCSF Custom Discovery
programs.subtitle: Research Platform

projects.name: IPI: Immunoprofiler Consortium
projects.card: Coordinates handling of human biopsy samples from cancer patients and performs deep tests of immune composition, gene expression, and interaction biology — treating cancers as discrete immunopathologies.

projects.name: AutoIPI: AutoImmunoprofiler Consortium
projects.card: A consortium that profiled autoimmune diseases with proteomic, transcriptomic, epigenomic, and structural analyses of freshly collected tissue and matched blood, to find pathways, targets, and better patient selection.
partners: Co-investigators: Roose, Gross, Erle, Ye, Chan, Combes, Fragiadakis

projects.name: STAMP: Sjögren's Disease Team
projects.fullTitle: Sjögren's Team for Accelerating Medicines Partnership
projects.division: Oral Medicine, Oral Pathology & Oral Radiology
projects.card: Interrogates the tissue and systems biology of Sjögren's Disease using deep sequencing to understand pathogenesis, identify targets, and map progression from early to advanced disease.
projects.full: STAMP is the Sjögren's disease team of the Accelerating Medicines Partnership® Autoimmune and Immune-Mediated Diseases (AMP® AIM), managed by the Foundation for the NIH and led by UCSF. Across clinical sites at UCSF/UC Berkeley, Johns Hopkins, the Oklahoma Medical Research Foundation, and the NIDCR, the team deeply characterizes people with or at risk for Sjögren's disease, including healthy controls, long-term follow-up participants from earlier cohorts, and people with Sjögren's-lupus overlap. Salivary gland biopsies, blood, saliva, and tears are analyzed with single-cell and spatial technologies to understand how the disease develops and progresses, how immune cells interact with salivary gland tissue, and which pathways could become new treatment targets.
projects.population: People with signs or symptoms of Sjögren's disease; healthy controls; prior SICCA/OMRF participants; Sjögren's-lupus overlap

projects.name: Tuberculosis Susceptibility Pathways
projects.card: The Suliman group uses systems biology — GWAS, transcriptomics, metabolomics, eQTLs — to identify pathways that determine why only 5–10% of exposed individuals develop active TB.

projects.name: Sepsis & ARDS Inflammatory Subtypes
projects.division: Pulmonary, Critical Care, Allergy & Sleep Medicine
projects.card: The Calfee Lab classifies ARDS and sepsis patients into validated hyper- and hypoinflammatory phenotypes, then queries immunophenotype and metagenomic differences in blood and tracheal aspirate.

projects.name: Arthritogenic T Cells in Rheumatoid Arthritis
projects.fullTitle: Immune Mapping of Arthritogenic Cells in Rheumatoid Arthritis
projects.card: A hypothesis-driven study of antigen-activated CD4 T cells in RA synovial tissue, plus a broad characterization of immune and non-immune cells in the synovium — toward more targeted therapeutics.
projects.full: In rheumatoid arthritis, it is hard to tell which T cells in an inflamed joint are actually responding to a self-antigen and which are simply caught up in the inflammation. Dr. Ashouri's lab showed that NUR77, a protein switched on only when a T cell recognizes its antigen, marks these disease-driving cells. This pilot collects synovial tissue (and, when possible, joint fluid) with matched blood and serum from about 12 patients with seropositive rheumatoid arthritis undergoing joint surgery. The team uses spectral flow cytometry and single-cell sequencing with T and B cell receptor sequencing to find antigen-activated lymphocytes and their receptors, profiles all immune and non-immune cells in the joint, and measures autoantibodies and cytokines in blood.
partners: ImmunoX CoLabs (Disease to Biology, Data Science)
projects.population: Adults with seropositive rheumatoid arthritis undergoing a joint procedure (e.g., joint replacement, synovectomy)

projects.name: GI Cancer Organoid Biobank
projects.fullTitle: Predictors of Response to Systemic Therapy in Pancreatic, Colorectal, and Intestinal Cancers
projects.funding: Foundation · Mark Foundation for Cancer Research (Endeavor Award); Shorenstein Award
projects.card: A living biobank of patient-derived organoids from pancreatic, colorectal, and small-intestinal cancers, paired with blood and normal tissue, to study metastasis and predict response to systemic therapy.
projects.full: This project generates, characterizes, and banks 3D tumor organoids from patients with pancreatic, colorectal, and small-intestinal (jejunal, duodenal, ampullary) cancers, with a target of 240 patients. Fresh tumor from biopsies and surgeries, along with ascites or pleural fluid, adjacent normal tissue, and blood, are collected. Patient immune cells are added back to the organoids to create 'ImmunoOrganoids,' allowing researchers to study how cancers progress to metastasis, which immune patterns predict response to therapy, and how tumors respond to EGFR- and Ras-targeted drugs. Organoids remain at UCSF.
partners: UCSF Molecular Profiling in GI Malignancies Biorepository (Cancer Center Tissue Core)
projects.population: Patients with pancreatic, colorectal, or small-intestinal cancer undergoing biopsy, surgery, thoracentesis, or paracentesis

projects.name: Spatial Map of Autoimmune Hepatitis
projects.fullTitle: Profiling Molecular Mechanisms of Autoimmune Hepatitis in the POSULD Cohort
projects.card: Mapped where immune cells and liver cells interact in autoimmune hepatitis, using spatial gene mapping and imaging of liver biopsies from a diverse San Francisco patient cohort.
projects.full: Autoimmune hepatitis is an understudied chronic liver disease that disproportionately affects women and people of color. Building on the POSULD cohort at Zuckerberg San Francisco General and UCSF (about 300 participants, 60 with autoimmune hepatitis) and earlier work that pointed to a possible autoantigen (AFF3) and to B and T cell interactions through CD40, this seed project mapped liver biopsies from patients with autoimmune hepatitis and a comparison liver disease (MASLD). The team used spatial transcriptomics with a custom 480-gene liver panel and multiplexed immunofluorescence to see where AFF3-expressing liver cells and CD40/CD40L-expressing immune cells sit, and piloted single-cell profiling of matched blood samples.
partners: ImmunoX CoLabs (Disease to Biology, Biological Imaging Development)
projects.population: POSULD participants with autoimmune hepatitis, with MASLD participants as comparison

projects.name: Single-Cell Map of Lupus
projects.fullTitle: Mapping the cell-type-specific molecular and genetic basis of lupus using single cell multiomics
projects.card: Uses single-cell technologies to map which immune cells and genetic variants drive lupus in a diverse group of patients and controls, including how blood immune cells change during flares.
projects.full: Lupus (systemic lupus erythematosus) affects many organs, is far more common in women and in people of Asian, African, and Hispanic ancestry, and responds unevenly to treatment. Using blood samples from the ancestrally diverse California Lupus Epidemiology Study (CLUES), this project applies multiplexed single-cell technologies that read each immune cell's chromatin, genes, and surface proteins in about 300 patients and 80 controls. These data are combined with genetic studies to pinpoint which lupus-linked DNA variants act in which cell types, with a subset tested in T cells using CRISPR. Patients are also followed through flares and treatment, including a pilot of self-collected fingertip blood sampled frequently over time, to find markers that could guide more personalized care.
projects.population: Adults with lupus in the multiethnic CLUES cohort (including patients sampled at flare) and healthy controls

projects.name: SICCA: Sjögren's Registry & Biorepository
projects.fullTitle: Sjögren's International Collaborative Clinical Alliance
projects.division: Oral Medicine, Oral Pathology & Oral Radiology
projects.funding: NIH · NIDCR U01DE028891 (SICCA-NextGen); supplemental funding from the Sjögren's Foundation
projects.card: OCR manages data for SICCA, an international registry and biorepository of clinical data and biospecimens from people evaluated for Sjögren's disease, shared with researchers worldwide.
projects.full: The Sjögren's International Collaborative Clinical Alliance (SICCA) was established in 2003 with NIDCR funding to develop new classification criteria for Sjögren's disease and better characterize how it looks and what genes drive it. Between 2003 and 2013, the Alliance built the International Sjögren's Syndrome Biorepository and Data Registry: uniform clinical data and biospecimens collected at nine research sites around the world. Since 2020, SICCA-NextGen has used these existing data and specimens, along with genome-wide genotyping of all participants, to study how genes are switched on and off in Sjögren's at the cell and tissue level. Researchers worldwide can apply for SICCA biospecimens and data. OCR supports SICCA's data management and dissemination; specimen collection was completed years before OCR's involvement.
partners: Nine international research sites (incl. University of Buenos Aires
projects.population: People evaluated for Sjögren's disease at nine international research sites

projects.name: T-Cell Repertoire in GI Cancers
projects.fullTitle: Assessing the Immune Cell Repertoire of Pancreatic and Colorectal Cancer Patients
projects.card: Shennon Bio mapped the immune cell (T-cell receptor) repertoires of patients with pancreatic and colorectal cancer, using tumor tissue and blood collected through a UCSF biorepository.
projects.full: This project assessed the immune cell repertoire of pancreatic and colorectal cancer patients. Tumor tissue, blood, and de-identified clinical data were obtained through the UCSF Molecular Profiling in GI Malignancies Biorepository under an approved specimen request, without the need for personal health information.
partners: UCSF Molecular Profiling in GI Malignancies Biorepository (Cancer Center Tissue Core)
projects.population: Patients with pancreatic or colorectal cancer

projects.name: Nasal Immune Responses to Allergy Shots
projects.fullTitle: Local adaptive immune responses during allergen immunotherapy
projects.card: A pilot using simple nasal swabs to sample immune cells in the adenoids and nasal lining of people with airborne allergies, to learn how allergy shots retrain the immune system.
projects.full: Allergen immunotherapy (allergy shots) reduces symptoms of airborne allergies and allergic asthma, but how it changes the immune system is unclear, because most studies have looked only at blood. This seed project uses a non-invasive nasal swab, adapted from COVID research at the La Jolla Institute for Immunology, to sample the adenoids, a lymph tissue at the back of the nose, along with a paired swab of the nasal lining. Swabs from up to 12 patients at the UCSF Allergy and Immunology Clinic, comparing people about to start immunotherapy with those on long-term maintenance, are profiled with flow cytometry and single-cell sequencing of B and T cells. The goal is to show this approach works and lay the groundwork for following patients over time.
partners: Shane Crotty (La Jolla Institute for Immunology)
ImmunoX CoLabs (Disease to Biology, Flow Cytometry, Genomics, Data Science)
projects.population: Patients with airborne (aeroallergen) allergies at the UCSF Allergy and Immunology Clinic, before starting or on maintenance allergen immunotherapy

projects.name: Obesity and GLP-1 Biobank
projects.fullTitle: Development of an Obesity and Immune-Mediated Disease Pipeline
projects.card: Collects blood, fat tissue, and stool from diverse adults at Zuckerberg San Francisco General to study how obesity, GLP-1 drugs, and weight-loss surgery affect autoimmune and inflammatory diseases.
projects.full: This pipeline builds a biobank at Zuckerberg San Francisco General, a safety-net hospital serving a racially, ethnically, and socioeconomically diverse population often missing from obesity and immunology research. Adults with and without obesity, and with or without autoimmune or inflammatory conditions such as rheumatoid arthritis, lupus, type 1 diabetes, Graves' disease, and myositis, donate blood, fat tissue (by small biopsy or from planned surgery), and stool, along with health, diet, and quality-of-life questionnaires and an optional body-composition scan. People starting a GLP-1 medication or having weight-loss surgery give repeat stool samples over six months. The initial pilot aims to enroll 50 to 60 participants in its first year, and samples are open to UCSF investigators studying inflammation, metabolism, the microbiome, and immune-mediated disease.
sites: Zuckerberg San Francisco General (Endocrine, Rheumatology, and Ward 92 specialty clinics)
projects.population: Adults 18–75 at ZSFG or affiliated UCSF clinics, with or without obesity and with or without autoimmune disease, including people starting GLP-1 therapy or having bariatric surgery

projects.name: NICU/PICU Biobank
projects.card: Offered families who lost a child at UCSF Benioff Children's Hospital the chance to donate tissue to research, helping fill a major gap in understanding how organs like the brain develop in childhood.
projects.full: Families whose child passed away in the Children's Hospital had no way to donate tissue to research. Studies with parents who have lost a baby show that donation can bring meaning and help with grief and coping. Children have long been underrepresented in research, and childhood is largely missing from tissue atlases; for example, brain blood vessel cells have been described before birth and in adults, but not in children. This pipeline set out to collect brain tissue across pediatric ages with autopsy and neuropathology support, with the longer-term aim of a dedicated program serving researchers who study development across childhood.
partners: NICU/PICU and Labor & Delivery research coordinators
projects.population: Infants and children who pass away at UCSF Benioff Children's Hospital, with family consent

projects.name: Prostate Cancer Biobank
projects.card: Collects fresh tumor, tumor-adjacent, and normal tissue from prostate cancer surgeries to find molecular signs of aggressive disease and grow patient-derived organoids.
projects.full: This pipeline collects three to four fresh research samples from each prostatectomy for locally advanced prostate cancer, marked as tumor, tumor-adjacent, and distant normal tissue, plus lymph node metastases when available (about one set every two weeks). Samples are placed in growth media for culture and molecular profiling, including deep DNA and RNA sequencing, possible cell-surface protein profiling, spatial analysis, and patient-derived organoids. The goal is to understand how normal and pre-cancerous prostate tissue evolves into clinically significant cancer, find biomarkers in nearby normal tissue that predict aggressive or treatment-resistant disease, and expand UCSF's biobank of patient-derived prostate cancer models.
specimens: Fresh prostatectomy tissue (tumor, tumor-adjacent, distant normal)
projects.population: Patients with locally advanced prostate cancer undergoing prostatectomy

projects.name: Bronchiectasis & NTM Research Registry & Biorepository
projects.division: Pulmonary, Critical Care, Allergy & Sleep Medicine
projects.card: A growing cohort and biobank of blood, sputum, nasal brushings, and bacterial isolates from a diverse group of adults with bronchiectasis and NTM lung disease, shared with researchers studying these understudied diseases.
projects.full: INTEGRATE launched a prospective cohort and biobank in 2024; about 120 participants have since donated blood. With pipeline funding, the biobank is expanding from the Lung Health Center at Parnassus to the Chest Clinic at Zuckerberg San Francisco General, with a focus on groups underrepresented in research, and adding sputum and nasal brushings alongside blood (PBMCs, serum, plasma), NTM bacterial isolates, and yearly quality-of-life and social-needs questionnaires. The goal is to enroll 75 more participants. Samples support studies of how NTM bacteria and the immune system interact to cause lung disease, new bronchiectasis subtypes in diverse populations, and how CFTR-related disorders affect immune responses to NTM. OCR is helping upgrade sample tracking and the database, and a research website for sample requests is planned.
projects.population: Adults with bronchiectasis and/or NTM lung disease in INTEGRATE clinics, with a focus on groups underrepresented in research

projects.name: Colorectal Cancer Organoids for Immunotherapy
projects.fullTitle: Preclinical Testing of Immunotherapies in Combined CRC Air-Liquid Interface Patient-Derived Organoids plus Lymphoid Organoids
projects.card: Builds combined tumor and lymph-node organoids from colorectal cancer surgeries to test new immunotherapies, such as Treg depleters and CAR T cells, for the many colorectal cancers that don't respond to current immunotherapy.
projects.full: Immunotherapy helps only a small share of colorectal cancer patients. This feasibility study collects fresh tumor and lymph node tissue from colorectal cancer surgeries (10 cases in year 1) to build combined tumor and lymphoid organoids. These lab-grown models are used to test emerging immunotherapies, including CCR8 Treg depleters and GCC19 CAR T cells, measuring cancer cell killing and changes in the tumor's immune 'hubs' with spatial profiling. A larger multi-year effort is planned if the approach proves feasible.
partners: UCSF Molecular Profiling in GI Malignancies Biorepository (Cancer Center Tissue Core)
projects.population: Colorectal cancer patients (any stage) undergoing surgical resection; excludes rectal tumors after neoadjuvant chemoradiation

projects.name: Kidney Cancer Immunoprofiling
projects.fullTitle: Immunoprofiling of Renal Cell Carcinoma
projects.card: A pilot that profiles immune cells in kidney tumors removed during surgery and tests drug combinations on living tumor slices, aiming to match immunotherapies to each tumor's immune type.
projects.full: Single-drug treatments often fail in kidney cancer. This pilot collects tumor tissue and matched blood from 15 patients undergoing radical nephrectomy. Part of each tumor is profiled by flow cytometry to assign it to one of two immune 'archetypes,' and thin slices of living tumor are cultured with different drug combinations and analyzed by flow cytometry and single-cell sequencing. The goal is to find combinations that work for each archetype, laying the groundwork for a future clinical trial.
projects.population: Adults undergoing radical nephrectomy for kidney tumors larger than 5 cm

projects.name: Tissue-Resident T Cells in Psoriatic Arthritis
projects.fullTitle: Paired Synovial, Skin, and Blood Biospecimen Collection to Characterize Tissue-Resident Memory T Cells in Psoriatic Arthritis and Spondyloarthritis
projects.card: Collects paired joint (synovial) tissue, skin, and blood from patients with psoriatic arthritis and spondyloarthritis to study tissue-resident memory T cells as a potential treatment target.
projects.full: In partnership with Radera, this project enrolls about 12 patients with psoriatic arthritis or spondyloarthritis from UCSF rheumatology clinics who are having a large-joint procedure. Synovial tissue and blood are collected at the procedure, and a skin biopsy about two weeks later. Samples are fixed, banked, or delivered fresh with coded IDs only, so the sponsor can examine tissue-resident memory T cells using multiplex immunofluorescence and flow cytometry.
projects.population: Adults with psoriatic arthritis or spondyloarthritis scheduled for a large-joint procedure

projects.name: COPA Syndrome Biomarker Study
projects.fullTitle: Non-IMP clinical study to generate data on the natural history of disease, biomarkers, and relevance of clinical endpoints in patients with selected type 1 interferonopathies
projects.division: Pulmonary, Critical Care, Allergy & Sleep Medicine
projects.card: Follows children and adults with COPA syndrome and related rare interferon diseases for two years to track how the disease changes and which blood markers reflect disease activity.
projects.full: COPA syndrome and related type 1 interferonopathies (Aicardi-Goutières syndrome, SAVI, and familial chilblain lupus) are ultra-rare inherited diseases in which an overactive interferon pathway drives inflammation in the lungs, skin, joints, and other organs. There are no approved treatments. This multicenter study gives no study drug: at least 40 children and adults (about 10 with COPA syndrome) receiving standard care are followed for two years, with regular visits measuring an interferon gene score, doctor and patient assessments, lung function, and skin and joint activity. An optional interview substudy captures what matters most to patients and families. The results will help design trials of new therapies.
projects.eligibility: Children and adults with a genetic diagnosis of COPA syndrome, AGS, SAVI, FCL, or another selected type 1 interferonopathy

projects.name: COPA Syndrome Natural History Study
projects.fullTitle: Natural History Study of Selected Type 1 Interferonopathies with Mutation in cGAS/STING Pathway
projects.division: Pulmonary, Critical Care, Allergy & Sleep Medicine
projects.card: Reviewed medical records of patients with COPA syndrome and related rare interferon diseases to describe how these conditions are diagnosed, progress, and are treated in real-world care.
projects.full: COPA syndrome and related type 1 interferonopathies are ultra-rare inherited inflammatory diseases with little published information on how they unfold over time. This multinational study reviewed existing medical records at expert centers to describe patients' characteristics at diagnosis, how the disease changed afterward, the treatments and healthcare they received, and survival, with a goal of about 125 patients across all included syndromes. No visits or procedures were required. The findings support the design of future trials for new therapies.
projects.eligibility: Patients of any age with a genetically confirmed type 1 interferonopathy in the cGAS/STING pathway, identified from site medical records

projects.name: POETYK SjS-1: Deucravacitinib for Sjögren's
projects.fullTitle: A Phase 3, Randomized, Double-blind, Placebo-controlled Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Deucravacitinib in Adults with Active Sjögren's Syndrome (POETYK SjS-1)
projects.card: A Phase 3 trial testing whether deucravacitinib, a pill already approved for psoriasis, reduces disease activity in adults with active Sjögren's disease compared with placebo.
projects.full: Sjögren's disease has no approved treatment that targets its underlying inflammation. This international Phase 3 study (about 756 participants) tests deucravacitinib, an oral medicine approved for psoriasis that blocks inflammatory signals such as type I interferon and IL-12. Participants are randomly assigned to one of two doses or placebo for 52 weeks, with visits every four weeks that include saliva and tear measurements, joint exams, and blood and urine tests. Those who complete the first year may continue on active drug for up to two more years.
projects.intervention: Deucravacitinib oral tablet, two doses twice daily vs. placebo for 52 weeks; optional 2-year extension on active drug
projects.eligibility: Adults 18+ with moderate-to-severe active Sjögren's (anti-Ro/SSA positive, diagnosed within 10 years, some remaining saliva flow)

projects.name: DACAT: Cephalosporin Allergy Testing
projects.fullTitle: Optimizing the Diagnostic Approach to Cephalosporin Allergy Testing
projects.division: Pulmonary, Critical Care, Allergy & Sleep Medicine
projects.funding: NIH · NIAID U01AI184071 (investigator-initiated; lead site Massachusetts General Hospital)
projects.card: UCSF took part in a national trial using carefully supervised skin tests and drug challenges to find the best way to diagnose cephalosporin antibiotic allergy and learn which related antibiotics are safe.
projects.full: Cephalosporins are first-line antibiotics for pneumonia, urinary tract infections, and surgical infections, but there is no standard, validated way to test for cephalosporin allergy, so many people avoid useful antibiotics. DACAT is the first clinical trial in drug allergy to compare diagnostic strategies for a major antibiotic class. About 300 participants at six U.S. sites, including UCSF during OCR's involvement, undergo double-blind skin testing and placebo-controlled drug challenges over two to four visits. The study aims to confirm or rule out suspected allergies, test whether skin testing is useful, measure cross-reactivity with related antibiotics, and investigate how cephalosporin allergy works.
projects.intervention: Double-blind skin testing and placebo-controlled drug challenges with cephalosporins (and amoxicillin)
projects.eligibility: People with a history of an immediate allergic reaction to at least one cephalosporin who are not currently taking beta-lactam antibiotics

projects.name: Epicel Cultured Epidermal Autografts (HUD)
projects.fullTitle: Epicel HUD-Cultured Epidermal Autographs (HUD)
projects.card: Provides Epicel, lab-grown sheets of a patient's own skin cells, under a Humanitarian Use Device approval to cover large, deep burns at UCSF Hyde Hospital.

projects.name: Long COVID Physiology
projects.fullTitle: Physiologic Characteristics of symptomatic Long-COVID patients
projects.card: Studies the physical and physiological characteristics of patients with ongoing Long COVID symptoms at UCSF Hyde and Stanyan Hospitals.

projects.name: Peritoneal Pull-Through Vaginoplasty
projects.fullTitle: Peritoneal Pull Through Technique for Gender Confirmation Vaginoplasty Grafting
projects.card: Evaluates the peritoneal pull-through technique as a grafting approach in gender-affirming vaginoplasty at UCSF Hyde Hospital.

projects.name: Papyrus Covered Coronary Stent (HUD)
projects.fullTitle: Papyrus Covered Coronary Stent System Humanitarian Use Device (HUD)
projects.card: Provides the Papyrus covered coronary stent under a Humanitarian Use Device approval to seal tears in heart arteries during procedures at UCSF Stanyan Hospital.

projects.name: TOPS: Motion-Preserving Spinal Implant
projects.fullTitle: A Clinical Study to Access the Safety and Effectiveness of the Premia Spine TOPS System
projects.card: A randomized study comparing the TOPS System, a motion-preserving spinal implant, with standard fusion surgery for lumbar spinal stenosis with slipped vertebrae, at UCSF Stanyan Hospital.
projects.full: Lumbar spinal stenosis, a narrowing of the spinal canal common with aging, causes back and leg pain that worsens with standing and walking. When a vertebra has also slipped forward (degenerative spondylolisthesis), surgeons usually fuse the affected segment after relieving pressure on the nerves. This FDA investigational device study, which enrolled 305 patients at sites across the U.S., compares the TOPS System, an implant designed to stabilize the spine while preserving motion, with standard transforaminal lumbar interbody fusion. Patients were randomly assigned 2:1 to TOPS or fusion and are followed for five years, with the main results assessed at two years.
projects.intervention: TOPS System (Total Posterior Spine) vs. transforaminal lumbar interbody fusion (TLIF), randomized 2:1
projects.eligibility: Adults 35–80 with at least moderate lumbar spinal stenosis and grade I degenerative spondylolisthesis at one level needing decompression surgery

projects.name: AIRTIVITY: BI 1291583 for Bronchiectasis
projects.fullTitle: A Phase III, Randomised, Double-blind, Placebo-controlled Study to Assess the Efficacy, Safety, and Tolerability of BI 1291583 2.5 mg Administered Once Daily for up to 76 Weeks in Patients With Bronchiectasis (The AIRTIVITY™ Study)
projects.division: Pulmonary, Critical Care, Allergy & Sleep Medicine
projects.card: A Phase 3 trial testing whether a once-daily pill, BI 1291583, reduces flare-ups in adults and adolescents with bronchiectasis compared with placebo.
projects.full: AIRTIVITY is a large international Phase 3 study (about 1,755 participants) of BI 1291583, a once-daily tablet, in people aged 12 and older with bronchiectasis who produce sputum and have had recent flare-ups. Participants are randomly assigned to BI 1291583 or placebo for up to 76 weeks, track their symptoms in a smartphone diary, and attend up to 10 clinic visits. The main measure is how often flare-ups occur in each group. The study is expected to finish in December 2027.
projects.intervention: BI 1291583 2.5 mg tablet once daily vs. placebo, up to 76 weeks
projects.eligibility: Ages 12+ with CT-confirmed bronchiectasis, chronic sputum, and recent flare-ups needing antibiotics

projects.name: CLEAR: AZD0292 for Bronchiectasis with Pseudomonas
projects.fullTitle: A Phase IIb Randomized, Double-blind, Placebo-controlled, Parallel, Multidose Study to Evaluate the Efficacy, Safety, and PK of AZD0292 in Participants 12 Years of Age and Older With Bronchiectasis and Chronic Pseudomonas Aeruginosa Colonization
projects.division: Pulmonary, Critical Care, Allergy & Sleep Medicine
projects.card: A Phase 2b trial testing AZD0292, an IV antibody treatment, to prevent flare-ups in people with bronchiectasis whose airways are chronically infected with Pseudomonas bacteria.
projects.full: CLEAR is a Phase 2b study (about 435 participants) of AZD0292, an antibody given by IV infusion, for preventing flare-ups in people aged 12 and older with bronchiectasis whose airways are chronically colonized with Pseudomonas aeruginosa, a bacterium linked to frequent flare-ups, declining lung function, and poorer quality of life. Two dosing regimens are compared with placebo. People with cystic fibrosis who carry Pseudomonas are included as a smaller exploratory group. The study is expected to finish in June 2028.
projects.intervention: AZD0292 (bispecific monoclonal antibody), IV, two dose regimens vs. placebo
projects.eligibility: Ages 12+ (at least 35 kg) with CT-confirmed bronchiectasis, recent flare-ups, and chronic Pseudomonas in the airways

projects.name: SOUNDS: Protecting Hearing During NTM Treatment
projects.fullTitle: Phase 2 Study of the Efficacy and Safety of ORC-13661 for the Prevention of Drug-Induced Hearing Loss in Patients Receiving Intravenous Amikacin Therapy for Non-Tuberculous Mycobacterium Disease
projects.division: Pulmonary, Critical Care, Allergy & Sleep Medicine
projects.funding: NIH · NIDCD U01DC020175 (lead site Oregon Health & Science University; sponsor-investigator Kevin Winthrop)
projects.card: A Phase 2 trial testing whether ORC-13661 can protect hearing in people receiving the antibiotic amikacin for nontuberculous mycobacterial (NTM) lung disease.
projects.full: Severe NTM lung infections are often treated with IV amikacin, an antibiotic that can damage the inner ear and cause hearing loss or balance problems. This Phase 2 study tests ORC-13661, an investigational pill taken alongside amikacin, to see whether it prevents or lessens that damage. About 105 participants at 5 sites are randomly assigned to a high dose, a low dose, or placebo for up to 90 days. Researchers also measure effects on speech understanding, balance, and hearing quality. The study is expected to finish in February 2028.
projects.intervention: ORC-13661 (oral), high or low dose vs. placebo, during IV amikacin for up to 90 days
projects.eligibility: Adults 18–79 with NTM infection starting IV amikacin for at least 30 days

projects.name: STRIDE-CAP: CAPVAXIVE Effectiveness Against Pneumonia
projects.fullTitle: A Test-Negative Case-Control Study to Evaluate the Effectiveness of V116, CAPVAXIVE™ Against Pneumococcal Pneumonia in Older Adults
projects.card: A Merck study of adults 65 and older hospitalized with pneumonia, comparing vaccination histories to measure how well the CAPVAXIVE vaccine prevents pneumococcal pneumonia.
projects.full: STRIDE-CAP is a large observational study in the United States and Canada (about 22,000 participants) measuring how well CAPVAXIVE, Merck's 21-valent pneumococcal vaccine for adults, prevents hospitalization for pneumococcal pneumonia in people aged 65 and older. No vaccine is given as part of the study. Adults hospitalized with community-acquired pneumonia, often identified in the emergency department, share medical record information such as vaccination history, chest imaging, and lab results, and provide a urine sample. Researchers then compare vaccination rates between people whose pneumonia was caused by bacteria strains covered by the vaccine and those whose pneumonia was not.
projects.intervention: None (observational; CAPVAXIVE received only through routine care)
projects.eligibility: Adults 65+ hospitalized with community-acquired pneumonia confirmed by symptoms and chest imaging

projects.name: ALPHA: Modzatinib for Oral Lichen Planus
projects.fullTitle: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Dose-Finding Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Modzatinib (ATI-2138) in Adult Participants with Biopsy-Proven Forms of Lichen Planus Not Adequately Controlled with Topical Therapies
projects.division: Oral Medicine, Oral Pathology & Oral Radiology
projects.card: A Phase 2 trial testing modzatinib, an investigational pill that calms overactive T cells, in adults with moderate-to-severe erosive oral lichen planus not controlled by topical treatments.
projects.full: Lichen planus is an inflammatory disease driven by T cells that affects about 1% of people worldwide. In the mouth, it can cause painful sores that make eating, speaking, and brushing teeth difficult, and there is no approved targeted treatment. This randomized, double-blind study compares two doses of modzatinib, an oral medicine that blocks two signals T cells rely on (ITK and JAK3), with placebo over 16 weeks in adults whose oral lichen planus is not controlled by topical therapy. The oral lichen planus group will enroll about 36 participants at roughly 15 sites in the United States and Europe; a group for skin (cutaneous) lichen planus is planned later.
projects.intervention: Modzatinib (ATI-2138) oral tablet, two dose levels vs. placebo, 16 weeks
projects.eligibility: Adults 18–75 with biopsy-confirmed, moderate-to-severe erosive oral lichen planus not adequately controlled with topical therapy
